properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Legacy SHA-family hash implementations shipped transitively in the dependency tree (sha.js ^2.4.0 provides SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256/SHA-384/SHA-512; the sha1 ^1.1.1 and hash.js 1.1.7 packages also ship SHA-1/SHA-2), pulled in by the ethers v5 / hardhat-toolbox toolchain. No direct application call site — the app's own hashing is Keccak-256 via @noble/hashes. Note SHA-1 is classically broken; SHA-2 members are post-quantum-acceptable hashes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA library shipped in the dependency tree (via ethers v6 and its @types). Ethereum account control — the wallet contract's `owner` address and the hardhat deployment key — is ECDSA/secp256k1 and is quantum-vulnerable under Shor; this repo exists to layer PQ WOTS+ ownership on top of it. The library itself is the transitive dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey ^1.0.3 — OpenSSL's legacy EVP_BytesToKey key-derivation routine (MD5-based) as an npm package, a transitive dependency of the crypto-browserify/cipher-base polyfill stack used by the hardhat toolchain. Weak legacy KDF present in the shipped tree; no application call site found. Presence is the inventory question; use is not.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 implementations declared in the shipped dependency tree — the same algorithm asset whose explicit @noble/secp256k1/@types/secp256k1 lockfile entries are recorded under ALG-673c8f24 (elliptic 6.6.1 also provides secp256k1 ECDSA). This is the classical half of the wallet's dual design: the ECDSA/secp256k1 owner path that the post-quantum WOTS+ layer is built to supplement. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 implementations available in the shipped tree via transitive dependencies (tweetnacl ^1.0.3, @noble/curves via ethers v6). No application import or call site in this repo — surface availability of the library, not use. Ed25519 is quantum-vulnerable under Shor (migration would be ML-DSA-65) but nothing here exercises it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA implementations shipped in the dependency tree (@noble/secp256k1 via ethers v6; elliptic 6.6.1/^6.5.2 via the older ethers v5 stack). Unlike the other transitive algorithm entries, ECDSA/secp256k1 IS exercised by this codebase's operational model: the wallet contract's `owner` is an ECDSA Ethereum address, and the deployer/relay accounts configured in hardhat.config.ts sign with secp256k1 ECDSA — the exact exposure the PQ WOTS+ layer exists to mitigate. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: NIST P-256 (secp256r1) ECDSA/ECDH surface shipped via @noble/curves in the transitive tree (ethers v6 toolchain). No application call site found — library surface availability only. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor if ever exercised.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman capability shipped via transitive crypto libraries (elliptic 6.6.1, tweetnacl, @noble/curves) in the hardhat/ethers toolchain. No key-agreement call site exists in the application — this SDK signs and verifies but performs no ECDH. Surface availability only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key-agreement capability shipped transitively (tweetnacl box, @noble/curves via ethers v6). No application call site — the SDK does no key agreement. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor if ever exercised; migration would be ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's SHA-3/Keccak variant) is the hash backbone of the entire post-quantum WOTS+ design in this SDK: QuipSigner derives its quantum secret with keccak_256 (src/index.ts:82), instantiates WOTSPlus with keccak_256 as the hash function (src/index.ts:81), and hashes WOTS messages (src/index.ts:231); the Solidity contracts mirror it with keccak256(messageHash) in WOTSPlus.WinternitzMessage on QuipWallet.sol:73/104/130. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 KDF packages shipped transitively: @ethersproject/pbkdf2 5.8.0 (ethers v5 keystore layer, pulled by the hardhat toolchain), pbkdf2 ^3.0.17 and @types/pbkdf2 ^3.0.0/^4.0.1. No application call site — this SDK does no password-based derivation. Presence in the shipped tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js 3.0.1 shipped transitively (used by the ethers keystore layer for wallet-file encryption). No application call site — the SDK does no password-based derivation. Memory-hard KDF; not quantum-relevant (KDF), recorded as dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 module of the directly-declared @noble/hashes ^1.7.1 dependency (package.json:56). The application imports only the sha3 module (keccak_256) from this library — SHA-256 is available in the shipped library but has no call site in the application. PQ-safe hash family.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 module of the directly-declared @noble/hashes ^1.7.1 dependency. Available in the shipped library; no application call site. BLAKE3 is a PQ-acceptable hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 module of the directly-declared @noble/hashes ^1.7.1 (package.json:56) — this is the module the application actually imports (src/index.ts:31 `import { keccak_256 } from "@noble/hashes/sha3"`), providing both keccak_256 (Ethereum flavor, used live) and sha3_256. The live Keccak-256 call sites are recorded under ALG-052c24b2; this entry records the declared provider of that capability.

properties.name: pqs:context

AES is PQ-acceptable (symmetric); recorded as library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 (tweetnacl secretbox) AEAD shipped via the transitive tweetnacl ^1.0.3 dependency (see LIB-0469707e). No application call site — no secretbox usage in this SDK. PQ-acceptable symmetric AEAD; recorded as dependency-tree surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl ^1.0.3 / tweetnacl-util ^0.15.1 — transitive dependency declared in package-lock.json (required by another package in the hardhat/ethers toolchain), shipping XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox, X25519 and Ed25519 (recorded as ALG-f58a8f00/ALG-defedad1/ALG-683d5cd2). No application import of tweetnacl exists — the SDK's own crypto is @noble/hashes + @noble/ciphers + @quip.network/hashsigs. Presence in the shipped tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes ^1.7.1 — DIRECT dependency (package.json:56) and the hash backbone of this SDK: src/index.ts:31 imports keccak_256 from @noble/hashes/sha3 to instantiate the post-quantum WOTSPlus signer and derive the quantum secret; test files import the same. Also ships SHA-256, BLAKE3, SHA3-256, scrypt and pbkdf2 modules (recorded as separate ALG objects).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves — transitive dependency in the shipped tree (pulled by the ethers v6 toolchain), providing secp256k1, P-256, Ed25519, X25519 and ECDH surfaces (recorded as ALG-673c8f24/ALG-a6da3577/ALG-683d5cd2/ALG-defedad1/ALG-c9ffc8a8). No direct application import — library surface availability in the shipped build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ciphers ^1.2.1 — DIRECT dependency (package.json:55). The package also ships AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 modules (recorded as ALG-f61ec50f/ALG-c57b2423) which the application does not call.
